algorithm: Check if the graph can be colored with two colors such that no two adjacent vertices share the same color.
Perform a BFS or DFS traversal starting from an arbitrary vertex, assigning alternating colors (0 and 1).
If during traversal, an adjacent vertex has the same color as the current vertex, the graph is not bipartite.
If all vertices are colored without conflicts, the graph is bipartite.
edge_cases: Graph with a single vertex (n=1) is bipartite.
Graph with no edges (n vertices) is bipartite.
Graph with an odd-length cycle is not bipartite.
Graph with multiple connected components: each component must be bipartite for the entire graph to be bipartite.
parsed.inputs: n (integer >= 1) and edges (list of distinct [u,v] pairs where 0<=u<v<n)
parsed.output: True if the graph is bipartite, False otherwise
parsed.purpose: Determine if a simple undirected graph with n vertices (labeled 0 to n-1) and given edges is bipartite.
